text:
Tampa Bay won in overtime, and the win matched how the game was played. Victor Hedman's backhand at 2:07 of the extra period gave TBL a 4-3 win over SEA, and by the chance-quality numbers the home side had the better of it all night. TBL generated 3.68 expected goals to SEA's 2.67, put up 61 shot attempts to 47, and came out ahead in a 66-to-34 split of simulated replays. The Lightning were also better in every period, including the overtime, where they held a 0.39 to 0.04 edge.

Brandon Hagel carried the offense with both of his goals at even strength, the first tying it at 16:53 of the opening period after Ryan Winterton's backhand had put SEA up, and the second at 3:38 of the second. Hagel also led all skaters with 0.74 of his own expected goals, so the two goals were earned. Ilya Mikheyev's wrist shot at 9:58 of the third, a 23 percent chance, put TBL back in front after Jared McCann had tied it on the power play, and Matty Beniers answered with a tip-in at 15:41 to force the extra period.

SEA hung around through special teams and goaltending. The Kraken went 1 for 3 on the power play while TBL went 0 for 3, even though TBL's chances there (0.88 expected goals) were better than SEA's (0.46). Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 of 35 shots, including a 28 percent look from Pontus Holmberg in the first period, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 24 of 27. Both goalies finished slightly below expectation, which fits a game that stayed tied until Hedman broke it.
